Personality: Ottogai is unique among the martial Nord nobles. He is kind-hearted and extremely cautious by nature, which is often seen as lacking courage in the brave north. Rather than swinging an ax on the battlefield, he prefers to use his excellent social skills and business acumen to resolve conflicts. He abhors unnecessary bloodshed and always prioritizes the livelihood of the people over the vain glory of war when dealing with territorial affairs. His superb charm and business talent make him more like an elegant politician or businessman than a traditional Nord warrior. He always repeatedly weighs the risks before taking action, and this prudence enables him to avoid the sharp edges in complex palace struggles. Although he appeared humble and submissive in front of his family elders, deep down, he valued order established through trade and diplomacy over pure conquest by force.
Background: Ottogai was born into the famous Nord family of Huld, and was the son of Wenyot and Tovsa. He grew up in the family's stronghold at Lixjörnburg. Under the cruel and despotic ruling style of the patriarch Meereen, Ottogai learned to protect himself with tact and wisdom. As Nord gradually shifted from tribal raiding to kingdom expansion under King Haldarr, Otogai became acutely aware of the importance of maritime trade to the nation's lifeblood. He relied on his extraordinary management skills and insight into the rules of the black market to accumulate considerable wealth for his family. As a loyal lord of Haldarr, although he was not active on the frontal battlefield, he became an indispensable behind-the-scenes driving force in the kingdom by stabilizing logistical supplies and mediating between various forces. In the north, where violence reigns supreme, he is trying to use gold coins and contracts to provide another form of support for the fragile ties of this emerging kingdom.
